statement: Micron demonstrated what it calls the world's first 512GB DDR5 RDIMM, enabling up to 12TB of DRAM in a 24-slot dual-socket server, with volume production expected in the second half of 2027.
why: Denser server memory relieves a capacity constraint on large AI and database workloads and shows memory makers pushing TSV stacking capability beyond HBM.

impact.mechanism: Vertical interconnect packaging with through-silicon vias raises capacity per module, letting existing server footprints hold larger working sets that feed accelerator workloads.

evidence.excerpt: the successful demonstration of what it describes as the world's first 512GB DDR5 RDIMM (registered dual in-line memory module), validated across multiple server platforms
Micron expects the 512GB RDIMMs to be in volume production in the second half of 2027.

confidence.basis: Company press release distributed via a newswire, secondary tier, single publisher; the module is demonstrated but not yet in volume production.
